judgment.judgment: Major revision of acquired version proof chain
judgment.summary: Core normalization, refined comparison, current, translation and ray-kernel steps fail in explicit tests; final integrality and interpolation existence are not disproved.

findings.title: Integral fundamental-cycle normalization
findings.verified_check: For L=Q(zeta_3), d=1, Gamma={+1,-1}, Gamma'=1, homology transfer H0(Z)->H0(Z) is multiplication by 2, not onto. Over R=Z[zeta_3,1/3] the critical trivial coefficient line of weight barsigma-sigma would require evaluation coefficient 1/2.
findings.counterevidence: Torsion-free groups work; rational normalization works after inverting torsion order.
findings.impact: Scalar integral specialization and later congruence-unit descent need reproof.
findings.repair: Restrict to torsion-free groups or invert torsion order, then re-establish descent.

independent_verification.source_claim_check: Proposition2.27 permits finite-index unit subgroups with torsion; its normalization precedes later fixed-torsion-point specializations.
independent_verification.hypotheses_and_decisive_check: For L=Q(zeta3),Gamma={+-1},Gamma'=1,d1 and R=Z[zeta3,1/3], the relevant critical weight barsigma-sigma is trivial onGamma, while transfer on H0 is multiplication by2. A class normalizing to1 upstairs would require1/2, absent fromR. This tests the proposition's actual generality; it is not asserted that the identical example satisfies every subsequent fixed-point specialization.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: Torsion-free normalization or inversion of the torsion order removes this obstruction. Integral descent and the scalar specialization still need re-establishment.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: Retain Major for a core integral normalization step, without claiming all final integral values fail.

findings.title: Refined isogeny comparison omits degree
findings.verified_check: For square CM E/C, Gamma=1, f-ideal=(3), c=(2), alpha=beta=0, dual top pullback and ordinary top pullback each multiply by 3 while moment-zero bundle map is identity. Displayed comparison requires 9s(x)=s(x). Residues delta0-deltat yield a differential with two poles and at most two zeros, so some nonzero 3-torsion x has s(x)!=0.
findings.counterevidence: Connection and moment diagrams account for their own factors but not the inserted top form.
findings.impact: Theorem 4.9 invokes this comparison for integral denominator control; final Theorem 4.10 not disproved.
findings.repair: Restore degree in rational comparison; integral construction requires more than dividing by a nonunit.

independent_verification.source_claim_check: Theorem2.30/Proposition2.31 compare refined classes with both top-form pullbacks. The original differential/bundle conventions were checked, including the dual form convention.
independent_verification.hypotheses_and_decisive_check: For a square CM elliptic curve,Gamma1,[3],alpha=beta0, each ordinary and dual top-form pullback contributes3, while the moment-zero logarithm map is identity. The displayed comparison therefore demands9s(x)=s(x). A residue differential delta0-deltat for nonzero2-torsion has two poles and at most two zeros, so at least one of the eight nonzero3-torsion points has s(x) nonzero and is not a pole.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: The connection and moment maps do not supply the missing top-form degree. Restoring degree repairs the rational comparison; dividing by a nonunit is not an integral-construction repair.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: Retain Major for the refined comparison used in Theorem4.9 denominator control. Theorem4.10 itself is not disproved.

findings.title: Wrong binomial sign in explicit current
findings.location: Definition 3.15 p.37; Theorem 3.20 pp.39-41; binomial expansion p.41
findings.verified_check: d=1, E=C/(Z+iZ), Gamma=1, f=delta0-delta_(i/2), n=1, l=1 gives Fourier coefficient F=2. Printed inverse 1/a+u/a^2 multiplied by connection a+u gives 1+2u/a mod u^2; residual 4u/pi times chi_l vol is nonzero.
findings.counterevidence: Moment zero misses the defect; inserting (-1)^b repairs the local inverse.
findings.impact: Explicit representative and all subsequent sign-dependent formulas need audit; abstract residue class not disproved.
findings.repair: Insert alternating binomial sign and recompute holomorphic derivative and volume conventions.

independent_verification.source_claim_check: The explicit-current expansion is checked in the source's actual connection d+nu convention; its inverse coefficients omit alternating signs.
independent_verification.hypotheses_and_decisive_check: For d1,Gamma1,E=C/(Z+iZ),residue delta0-delta_(i/2), the l1 Fourier coefficient is2. At the first truncated logarithm order, (a+u)(1/a+u/a^2)=1+2u/a mod u^2, producing the reported nonzero Fourier residual. The same calculation with the alternating coefficient cancels it.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: Moment0 is insensitive to this error, and the abstract residue class is not disproved. The local inverse needs(-1)^b; every subsequent sign-sensitive current/holomorphic-derivative convention still needs audit.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: Retain Major for the explicit core representative and downstream formulas, with local repair distinguished from global normalization.

findings.title: Translation duplicates full residue pullback
findings.verified_check: Gaussian CM E, p=5, d=1, Gamma=1, n=1, c=(2), prime-to-5 nonzero 3-torsion x with nonzero zeroth coefficient F. At zero translations, full pullback f'=phi*f is kernel invariant; compatible formal bases and residue uniqueness make all five summand zeroth coefficients equal F. Formula requires F=5F.
findings.counterevidence: Weighted residue proof works with the function on a single c-torsion component extended by zero, not the full inverse image.
findings.impact: Theorem 5.23 and its uses in Corollary 5.25 and Theorem 5.27 need correction.
findings.repair: Replace right-side f' by component-supported f0 and redo pairing/local-factor checks.

independent_verification.source_claim_check: Equation(5.5.1) defines f' on the full inverse-image divisor as phi*f, not as a single component extended by0; Theorem5.23 sums all kernel translates.
independent_verification.hypotheses_and_decisive_check: Take the ordinary Gaussian CM elliptic curve atp5,an etale degree5 isogeny,Gamma1,n1,c=(2), and a prime-to5 nonzero3-torsion point with nonzero zeroth residue coefficientF. At zero translations, full pullback f' is kernel-invariant. With the actual transported canonical formal/differential bases, residue uniqueness makes all five summands equalF, forcingF=5F. NonzeroF follows from the same two-poles/two-zeros argument; no extra divided trace is present at moment0.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: The weighted residue proof instead works with component-supported f0. Substituting f0 and redoing pairings/local factors is a repair obligation, not a fully verified replacement p-adic identity.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: Retain Major for the translation formula used by Corollary5.25 and Theorem5.27, without claiming nonexistence of the intended measure.

findings.title: Wrong units in ray-class kernel
findings.location: Theorem 5.27 Step 1 pp.74-75, exact sequence and (5.7.1)
findings.verified_check: L=Q(i), f=(3), p=5: O_f^*=1, O_L^*=C4, class number one. |Cl(3)|=2, |Cl(3*5^n)|=32*5^(2n-2); true kernel size 16*5^(2n-2), printed quotient size 4*5^(2n-2).
findings.counterevidence: Full-unit quotient is correct for trivial tame conductor in Step 3.
findings.impact: The group used for main measure pushforward loses finite characters.
findings.repair: Use closure of O_f^* consistently in G, q and pushforward, then redo interpolation.

independent_verification.source_claim_check: Theorem5.27 Step1 uses full units in the ray-kernel quotient at nontrivial tame conductor, whereas the relevant units must be congruent to1 modulo that conductor.
independent_verification.hypotheses_and_decisive_check: For Q(i),f=(3),p5, full unitsC4 inject modulo3 and congruence units are1. Class number1 gives |Cl(3)|=2 and |Cl(3*5^n)|=32*5^(2n-2). The true transition kernel has order16*5^(2n-2); dividing the p-adic units byC4 instead gives4*5^(2n-2), losing factor4 and finite characters.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: The full-unit quotient is valid when tame conductor is trivial, as in Step3. At generalf, use the closure of congruence units consistently and reprove pushforward/interpolation.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: Retain Major because the wrong kernel is used for the main measure construction, not because a corrected interpolation theorem has been disproved.

findings.title: Weight invariants require torsion-free module
findings.verified_check: R=Z[zeta_3,1/3], M=R/2R=F4 of weight 3sigma, Gamma=O_L^*. All unit cubes act as 1 mod2, so M^Gamma=M. Weight at -1 is -1 over R, so it is not in HChar_L(Gamma); printed direct sum is zero.
findings.counterevidence: Later differential modules are locally free over a domain.
findings.impact: Broad auxiliary proposition false; later locally free decompositions not refuted.
findings.repair: Add R-torsion-free hypothesis or weightwise annihilator condition.

independent_verification.source_claim_check: Proposition1.5 is stated for arbitrary coefficient modules, without a torsion-free condition.
independent_verification.hypotheses_and_decisive_check: R=Z[zeta3,1/3],M=R/2R of weight3sigma andGamma=all six units give M^Gamma=M: every unit cube acts as1 mod2. But the character takes-1 at-1 overR and is excluded from the printed HChar sum, making that sum0.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: An R-torsion-free hypothesis or the correct weightwise annihilator condition fixes the argument. Later differential modules are locally free over a domain.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: Retain Minor for an overbroad auxiliary proposition; the inspected locally free uses are not refuted.

findings.title: Completed and uncompleted residues confused
findings.verified_check: Square Epstein K(s)=4 zeta(s) beta(s): K(0)=-1 holomorphic, residue at0=0, at1=pi. Printed -1 and 1 are residues of pi^(-s) Gamma(s) K(s).
findings.counterevidence: Mellin proof and later current formulas use completion.
findings.impact: Local analytic normalization needs correction; not a general functional-equation audit.
findings.repair: State pole and residue claims for completed function.

independent_verification.source_claim_check: Proposition3.13 attributes completed Mellin pole/residue data to the uncompleted series.
independent_verification.hypotheses_and_decisive_check: The square Epstein test K(s)=4zeta(s)beta(s) has K(0)=-1 holomorphic and residue at1 equalpi. The completed pi^-s Gamma(s)K(s) instead has residues-1 at0 and1 at1, exactly explaining the missing completion.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: The Mellin proof and later current formulas use the completion. State the residue claim for that completed function; no wider functional-equation audit is asserted.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: Retain Minor for the local analytic normalization.

findings.title: Subgroup change ignores coset stabilizer
findings.verified_check: L=Q(i), Gamma=+-1, Gamma'=1, Lambda=Z+iZ, t=1/10, alpha=2,beta=0,s=2. Every orbit in Lambda+-t has one representative in Lambda+t; even summand gives equal series instead of factor2. Leading term10^6 and tail<16 prove nonzero.
findings.counterevidence: Fixed torsion coset gives original index; full orbit sums may restore aggregate factor.
findings.impact: Auxiliary lemma quantifiers false; not all later aggregate formulas refuted.
findings.repair: Use [Gamma_t:Gamma_t intersect Gamma'] or add fixed-coset hypothesis.

independent_verification.source_claim_check: Definition3.24/Lemma3.25 allow the relevant torsion coset to move underGamma, but use the full subgroup index rather than its stabilizer.
independent_verification.hypotheses_and_decisive_check: For Q(i),Gamma={+-1},Gamma'=1,Lambda=Z+iZ,t1/10,alpha2,beta0,s2, every orbit of the two-coset union has one representative inLambda+t. The even summand therefore gives equal series instead of factor2. The leading term10^6 and tail bound<16 prove this series is nonzero.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: Use [Gamma_t:Gamma_t intersect Gamma'] or impose a fixed-coset condition. Later sums over all cosets can recover aggregate factors and are not all declared false.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: Retain Minor for an auxiliary quantifier defect.

findings.title: Universal critical-value nonvanishing false
findings.location: Corollary 4.15 and Remark 4.16 p.54; repetition p.55
findings.verified_check: E5:y^2=x^3-25x has CM by Z[i], Hecke character psi5 of type sigma. chi=psi5/N has critical type -barsigma. L_f(chi,0)=L(E5,1)=0 by root number -1. Nonzero period quotient is zero, outside Qbar^*.
findings.counterevidence: Period comparison remains a nonzero-period comparison; Theorem4.10 allows zero.
findings.impact: Side nonvanishing assertion false without disproving algebraicity/integrality.
findings.repair: Replace Qbar^* by Qbar for L-value or assume nonvanishing.

independent_verification.source_claim_check: Corollary4.15/Remark4.16 place the universally normalized critical value in the multiplicative group, thereby excluding0.
independent_verification.hypotheses_and_decisive_check: E5:y^2=x^3-25x is the Gaussian CM twist; for chi=psi5/Norm of critical type-barsigma, L_f(chi,0)=L(E5,1)=0 by the negative functional-equation root number. The period is nonzero, so the normalized value is0 and is outsideQbar*. This uses analytic functional equation and CM correspondence, not BSD.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: Theorem4.10 permits zero; the nonzero-period comparison is unaffected. ReplaceQbar* byQbar for this value, or add nonvanishing.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: Retain Minor for the side nonvanishing assertion, not a disproof of algebraicity or integrality.

findings.title: Injective descent need not be flabby
findings.verified_check: X=point, Gamma=Z, I=Map(Z,Q) with shift is coinduced injective. Its local system on S1 has global sections constant sequences Q and sections on an arc I; restriction is not surjective.
findings.counterevidence: Borel comparison itself holds; coinduced module is acyclic and difference equation solvable.
findings.impact: Auxiliary proof incorrect, standard comparison not refuted.

independent_verification.source_claim_check: AppendixA.2 asserts that descent of an injective equivariant sheaf is flabby.
independent_verification.hypotheses_and_decisive_check: For X=point,Gamma=Z,I=Map(Z,Q) with shift, coinduction of injectiveQ supplies an injective equivariant object. Its local system onS1 has global sections constant sequencesQ and sectionsI on a small arc; restriction is not onto, so the descended sheaf is not flabby.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: The shift-minus-identity equation is solvable, so the module remains acyclic and the Borel/group comparison can be justified by an acyclicity/descent argument. The comparison itself is not disproved.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: Retain Minor for an auxiliary proof step.

scope_questions.question: Integral pullback connection targeting phi*Omega_B for non-etale phi requires a divisibility or lift argument.
scope_questions.counterevidence: Zeroth-order degree counterexample is already closed; no separate higher-order counterexample established.

scope_questions.question: Reconcile Hodge types, multiplication-by-p versus Frobenius, coefficient pullback, and p^2 eta=p eta.
scope_questions.counterevidence: No counterexample to final formal commutative diagram established.

scope_questions.question: Integral character values and density need uniform norm/Kummer/divisibility evidence for bounded measure.
scope_questions.counterevidence: Polynomial derivative diagnostic disproves generic inference only, not boundedness of this pseudomeasure; cited de Shalit argument not fully checked.

i!=d overstatement; only i<d needed for low-degree conclusion.
Principal-generator tame congruence should be specified; no separate finding counted.

The three existing Needs Evidence items remain unresolved. No scientific TeX/PDF alteration is required.
